User runs a small homemade/artisanal business selling jams, candles, and soaps, primarily at local markets/events. They track sales and expenses, manage stock, and want to calculate earnings.

Recorded 2025 event sales:
- Mar 18, Downtown Farmers Market: $220
- Mar 25, Arts and Crafts Fair: $85
- Apr 1, Earth Day Market: $25
- May 6, Downtown Farmers Market: $350
- May 13, Mother’s Day Market: $200
- May 20, Foodie Festival: $400
Previously recorded gross total: $1,280. User later said they earned $420 at their most recent Downtown Farmers Market visit; treat this as a newer event, not clearly the May 6 sale, and calculate a new total only after confirming dates. Expenses remain unprovided, so net earnings are unknown.

Inventory: The recent Foodie Festival was successful and they cleared old stock. Candle stock is nearly sold out, and strawberry jam is a best-selling flavor. They have upcoming large orders and need help forecasting quantities, accounting for lead times, existing counts, sales data, supplier availability, seasonality, and safety stock. They are considering expanding artisanal soap varieties; advise using actual customer requests/sales data, testing demand, and checking production capacity, ingredient sourcing, and margins.

Customer retention: They plan a points-based loyalty program with tiered benefits. Rewards will include discounts and free products. They are considering a welcome incentive such as welcome points, a first-purchase discount, or a free item, while controlling reward costs. Promotion will use social media, email newsletters, market/in-store promotions, and trained staff explaining enrollment at checkout. Keep joining and tier rules simple and track performance.

Marketing/product expansion: They ordered 100 business cards as a cost-conscious starting quantity. They are considering gift baskets, including a possible “Downtown Farmers Market” themed basket using popular soaps and candles, branded packaging, a community note, themed token, and promo code. Start small and test demand. Do not imply permission to use the market’s name/branding; obtain organizer approval because it is a third-party event.
